When homeowners see a new HOA budget, one of their first questions is often: "What made this year different?"

Before walking through every expense category, explain the biggest changes from last year. It gives people a starting point for understanding the financial picture.

That's one of the conversations I built Budget Snapshot to support: https://budgetsnapshot.garrettsdevdesk.com

"Our HOA's expenses increased by $30,000" tells homeowners the result, but it leaves out the explanation.

Maybe insurance increased $18,000, planned maintenance added $10,000, and several smaller changes accounted for the rest.

Breaking the total into its biggest drivers helps people understand how the budget arrived at its new number.

An HOA budget line showing $80,000 for a service doesn't tell homeowners much about what changed.

Knowing that the same service cost $68,000 last year gives the number a useful reference point. Now there's a $12,000 difference worth explaining.

Year-over-year comparisons can make financial presentations much clearer.

Explore Budget Snapshot: https://budgetsnapshot.garrettsdevdesk.com

A spreadsheet can calculate the difference between last year's HOA budget and this year's. It can't always tell homeowners why that difference happened.

A contract renewed at a higher rate. Utility costs changed. A planned project began. A new vendor reduced expenses.

Try adding a short explanation beside each major budget change. The context is often what makes the number useful.

An increase in this year's HOA budget could be temporary, or it could affect the community's finances for years.

A one-time maintenance project may disappear next year. A higher annual service contract might become part of the new spending baseline.

That distinction is worth explaining when presenting financial changes.

Budget Snapshot: https://budgetsnapshot.garrettsdevdesk.com

Homeowners shouldn't have to compare two spreadsheets line by line just to understand why their HOA's budget changed.

Show the biggest differences, explain what caused them, and identify which expenses may continue into future years. Then let the detailed budget support the conversation.

When reviewing a budget, do you find a year-over-year comparison helpful?
